references.text: The tithe law in the Mosaic Law: "Every tenth of the land, whether from the produce of the soil or from the fruit of the trees, belongs to the Lord. It is holy to the Lord" ([ref:3 Mos 27:30|Leviticus 27:30]). The Pharisees were careful to give tithes, which Jesus confirms, but they neglected what was more important.

The tithe of the harvest is mentioned in [ref:5 Mos 14:22-23|Deuteronomy 14:22-23], which commands that one should give a tenth of all that the field produces. The Pharisees extended this to include even the smallest herbs.

The prophet Micah summarizes what God requires: "to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God" ([ref:Mi 6:8|Micah 6:8]). Jesus rebuked the Pharisees for neglecting exactly justice and God's love in favor of external details.

"For I desire mercy, not sacrifice" ([ref:Hos 12:6|Hosea 12:6]) – God values love and righteousness higher than outward religious acts, which corresponds to Jesus' point that the Pharisees neglected love for God.

Samuel said to Saul: "To obey is better than sacrifice, to listen is better than the fat of rams" ([ref:1 Sam 15:22|1 Samuel 15:22]). Obedience to God's will, including justice and love, weighs more heavily than outward religious actions.

The parallel passage in [ref:Matt 23:23|Matthew 23:23] contains Jesus' corresponding woe against the Pharisees: "You give a tenth of your mint, dill, and cumin, but you have neglected the more important matters of the law: justice, mercy, and faithfulness."
[ref:Matt 23:24|Matthew 23:24]: "Blind guides! You strain out a gnat but swallow a camel." This illustrates the same point about the Pharisees' misplaced priorities between the small and the great.
Jesus quotes Hosea: "I desire mercy, not sacrifice" ([ref:Matt 9:13|Matthew 9:13]). This emphasizes that God prioritizes inner attitudes such as love and mercy over outward religious actions.

The immediate context in [ref:Luk 11:39-41|Luke 11:39-41], where Jesus criticizes the Pharisees for cleaning the outside of the cup while being full of greed inside, builds up to the woe in verse 42 about outward piety without inner righteousness.

"Whoever does not love their brother whom they have seen cannot love God whom they have not seen" ([ref:1 Joh 4:20-21|1 John 4:20-21]). Love for God, which the Pharisees neglected, is also shown in love for others and in righteous action.
